title: The Names of Things
human_question: What is actually here, underneath the names we give it?
journey: Chathura looks at ordinary Sri Lankan life with fresh eyes: places, people, titles, and things, each carrying a name and a story told about it.
surface: The beauty and strangeness of the everyday. Moments where a name and the thing it names quietly come apart.
depth: The two truths: conventional (names, concepts) and ultimate (what is actually there). The four ultimate realities (mind, mental factors, matter, Nibbāna) and the full map of 121 types of mind. This group lays out the map the whole series unfolds; three ultimates are explored in Groups 2–9, and the fourth (Nibbāna) is reached only in Group 10.

arc.opening: The named world: a place, a person known by a role, a thing everyone recognises. Object 1 is acquired here.
arc.middle: Encounters where the label and the reality separate: a renamed village, a thing 'the same' though every part is replaced, a person larger than their title.
arc.closing: The first hint that experience itself is made of moments of mind, and the first thing found beneath the names is the pull of wanting.

hands_off: Once you look beneath the names, the first thing you meet is wanting.

concepts.role: Abhidhamma itself and the split between conventional truth (names) and ultimate truth (what is actually there), the lens for the whole series.
The four ultimate realities: mind, mental factors, matter, Nibbāna. Three are met across the series; the fourth is reached only in Group 10.
How mind is classified by plane and kind: the first sight of the map.
The full 121 types of consciousness: the whole map in one view, unfolded group by group.
The compendium of all things (aggregates, sense bases, elements, noble truths): what a 'person' is made of when the name is removed.
Concepts and names (paññatti): how names point to things, and names for things that do not ultimately exist.

unknowns: Film count is a draft; it is finalised in Step 4 (chronological slate).
Concept roles are English working glosses, not approved interpretations.

lesson.in_simple_terms: We live among names: mountains, mornings, boats, wells, grades and lanterns. These films show that a name is a useful shared agreement, but when you look closely at what it names you find parts, empty spaces and quick passing moments rather than one solid thing. Even the mind turns out to be a fast stream of moments, and the first thing that stirs beneath the names is wanting.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අප ජීවත් වන්නේ නම් මැද වන අතර ඒ නම් ප්‍රයෝජනවත් සම්මුති වුවත්, සමීපව බලන විට ඒවාට යටින් ඇත්තේ කොටස්, හිස් අවකාශ සහ ඉක්මනින් ඉපිද නැතිවන මොහොත් බව මේ චිත්‍රපට පෙන්වයි. සිතද එවැනි මොහොත් පෙළක් වන අතර, නම්වලට යටින් මුලින්ම හමුවන්නේ තණ්හාවයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma describes two ways of speaking about the same world: conventional teaching in everyday names, which the Buddha used so that people could understand easily, and ultimate teaching, which describes what is actually there. Names, and the wholes they call to mind (mountains, times, spaces, boats, persons), are concepts (paññatti): divide them and they disappear, as cloth dissolves into thread. What the texts say remains are the ultimate realities: mind, the mental factors that arise with it, matter, and Nibbāna, the first three described as momentary activities rather than solid things. Mind itself is a stream of brief moments of knowing, which the texts map into 121 types, and a person can be taken apart into five heaps of passing events, a sorting meant to loosen the habit of 'I' and 'mine', and which names craving as the cause of suffering.
progression: EPD-0001 One Mountain, Many Names: many names can point to one thing; a name is a shared agreement, not the thing itself.
EPD-0002 When Morning Begins: some names, like 'morning', point to nothing you can hold at all; time is a concept built on the movement of the sun.
EPD-0003 Learning the Map: the same naming turns inward; the mind is a stream of moments of knowing, mapped into 121 types and learned by heart.
EPD-0004 The Same Boat: the test of taking apart; a whole that keeps its name while every part changes is a concept, not an ultimate reality.
EPD-0005 The Well: a name can be given to an absence; the concept of space names an emptiness among changing matter.
EPD-0006 The Taster: what we know of a thing comes through the doors of the senses; knowing arises when a sense meets its object.
EPD-0007 The Ring of Fire: speed and seeing join separate moments into a whole that is not there, and the mind itself is such a stream.
EPD-0008 The Lantern: a person, like a lantern, is heaps of passing events; the point of seeing this is to loosen 'I' and 'mine', and wanting is found beneath the names.
lesson.builds_on: GRP-01 opens the series with wonder rather than doctrine: before any single state of mind is examined, it teaches the lens the whole journey uses, the difference between the names we live by and what is actually there, and it unfolds the full map of the mind that the following groups walk through region by region, with the fourth reality, Nibbāna, only named as a distant horizon.
lesson.hands_to_next: If names sit on top of passing moments, what in those moments makes us hold on? The group ends as the lantern comes down and leaves the next group to ask where wanting begins: in the pleasant feelings of the sense world, and in the kinds of mind rooted in greed.
